title: bls12-381-fixed-g2-invert-g1: STNFS in F_{p^12} with a packed-row slice sieve, certified thresholds and an exact fundamental domain, priced in Fp12-mul units

claims.statement: For every production instance (uniform nonidentity Q in G2, uniform z in GT, including z=1), the algorithm in proof.md returns P in G1 with e(P,Q)=z (P=infinity exactly for z=1) with success probability at least 0.39 over the uniform challenge and the algorithm's coins (>= 0.95 under the stated heuristics). The attack solves the GT discrete logarithm of z base g=e(P0,Q), a route the track rules admit, with a Special Tower Number Field Sieve in F_{p^12}: tower h = y^6 + y^3 + y^2 - y - 1 (Disc(h) = 23 x 2551 squarefree and h irreducible mod p are verified exactly, so O_h = Z[y]; u y a non-square in F_{p^6} is verified explicitly, so the tower is F_{p^12}), f = y^6 3p(x^2/y) mod h = x^12 - 2y x^10 + 2y^3 x^6 + y^5 x^2 + (1 + y - y^2 - y^3), g = x^2 + |u| y, with the x -> -x automorphism (aut 2). Relation collection is charged on an exact fundamental domain of the group generated by the units of O_h and the automorphism: canonical a = the least (Hermite normal form key of aO_h, Q_a, lexicographic) eligible a of its unit orbit (equal keys <=> unit multiples; no unit certificate), a5 > 0, Q_a(a) <= A^2/2 with A^2 = 2^21, and b in the half-slice Q_b(b) <= A^2 - Q_a(a), b5 >= 1; the canonical list is priced analytically at 2^90 units; non-primitive pairs (exact HNF test) are not credited. The factor base is the set of prime ideals of relative degree 1 over K_h with norm <= B on both sides (the only ones dividing a - bx for primitive pairs), including the ideals above K_h-primes of degree >= 2 such as the ramified norm-4 and norm-16 primes above 2 on the g side; a relation is a pair whose two ideals are B-smooth. The sieve runs one job per canonical a with the production-width kernel slice12.c: cells in packed rows (one 4-byte cell per point, no bounding-box bytes) with dense per-line suffix metadata, separately allocated segments of <= 2^62 bytes, segment-local 64-bit cell indices and 64-bit counters, exact recentring of every coset origin, one validated Barrett reduction for every modular step (p < 2^63), primes in [2^8, 2^20) applied line by line by 5-dimensional Schnorr-Euchner coset enumeration with direct updates, primes in [2^20, 2^63) by one 6-dimensional enumeration per sigma-pair emitting (segment-local cell, global 64-bit ideal id) records to retained per-segment stores with an apply pass, a scan against per-block thresholds and a recovery pass returning every sieved ideal of each survivor; the kernel is checked against brute force on every cell of slices of 2^18-2^24 cells with 1-10 segments. Thresholds come from nbound12.c: certified outward interval bounds on 16 log2 N_f and 16 log2 N_g per aligned 64-cell block (rational Rouche root disks of the four places of K_h, binary64 intervals widened by one ulp per operation, acceptance width 8 bits, unresolved single points rejected with their yield weight charged), bit-identical to its Python reference on all 2,401 pool rows; a cell passing the preliminary test has omitted mass <= slack + 8 bits, and a relation with omitted mass <= slack - (c+1)/16 bits and squarefree valuations at p >= 256 passes. Survivors are cofactorised with exact norms, trial division below 2^20, the recorded ideals and full-budget ECM to B on cofactors of <= slack + 8 bits using the measured 5-limb Montgomery multiplication of ecm12.c (367.76 instructions); a relation requires exact B-smoothness of both ideals. Every sieve constant is a callgrind executed-instruction count of the shipped kernels on linux/arm64 by the track's differential method, indexed by expected points per coset (line path 24.10-310.70 per update, record path 44.90-2231.66 per hit, apply 7.00 and recovery 7.003 per record, layout 12.325 and zero 0.625 per cell, scan 8.0 per cell + 21 per block, norm bounds 5,900 per evaluation at the measured 0.04232 evaluations per cell plus 4,200 per row). The retained yield is computed per pool row (20,000 exactly sampled eligible pairs regenerated from per-index seeds, 2,401 canonical, exact norms) as rho((log2 N_f + 5)/log2 B) rho((log2 N_g + 1)/log2 B) times the retentions of a finite Euler-product model of the distinct-sieved-prime threshold (small-prime mass, powers, quantisation; calibrated against exact smooth-number samples) times 0.99 per expected prime factor in (X2, B] for ECM misses, with exact rational lattice-count factors (yield x 2401/2500, work x 2601/2500). Filtering is a CADO-style purge + merge simulated on the production ideal-occurrence profile with the dense columns propagated through the merge at scale 2^17 (N/U = 0.0538 at row weight 100, excess 1.3), charged with a factor-2 pad on the dimension; linear algebra is block Wiedemann on the square sparse system with the Schirokauer-map columns as right-hand sides at 36 instructions per entry (shipped kernel la_mac.s, 33 per entry with 64-bit column indices) and row weight 100; two individual-log descents (boot on the index-p^6 subfield-coset lattice, then a dynamic programme over 2-bit size levels with explicit per-node costs on the ideal's own side, every child's subtree included, the measured ECM multiplication scaled quadratically in the limb count) are metered at a 2^106-unit cap (Markov abort <= 0.014). Operating point B = 2^69, X2 = 2^63, slacks (292, 220) bits, excess 1.3, A^2 = 2^21, theta = 1/2, alpha (5, 1): population 2^127.389 cells at 516.5 instructions per cell, retained relation orbits 2^64.219 against the required excess x U = 2^63.830 (U = 2^63.451 sigma-orbits of the factor base; +0.389-bit margin, 3.3 pool standard errors), relation collection 2^122.114 units, linear algebra 2^119.579 units (N = 2^60.23). Total work W <= 2^122.343600 target-group-operation equivalents (1 unit = one dense Fp12 multiplication = 20,000 AArch64 instructions), the full-ledger logarithm (evidence12.py prints total_log2W_full_ledger = 122.343555) rounded up: relcol 2^122.114 + LA 2^119.579 + descent cap 2^106 + canonical list 2^90 + Schirokauer maps 2^88 + factor base 2^72 + filtering/storage/misc 2^64 + verification 2^11. No preprocessing or advice beyond this charged work; peak memory is reported (2^72.88 bytes per a-slice job in segments of <= 2^62 bytes, plus 2^78 bytes of staging for the canonical list), not scored. All heuristics (H1-H7 of proof.md section 11) are disclosed with support, sensitivity and limitations. This is an analytic cost claim supported by exact-norm sampling, measured kernels, a calibrated retention model, a filtering simulation and a descent programme, not a full-size execution.

experiments.purpose: One stdlib-only run (imports model12.py, common12.py, threshold_model.py, ideal_canonical.py, embedding_bounds.py, lattice_count_bounds.py, filtsim.py, descent12.py; reads config.json, pool12-1.b85, pool12-2.b85, la_mac.s). [0] Res_y(h, f(x^2 -> -|u| y)) = 0 mod p exactly; [0b] h irreducible mod p and (u y)^((p^6-1)/2) = -1 in F_p[y]/h; [0c] field certificate (Disc(h) squarefree, h irreducible mod p, O_h = Z[y]). [1] Dickman rho vs reference values. [2] pool regeneration: the eligible pairs of seed 1 with indices 0..samples-1 are regenerated from their per-index seeds (uniform eligible a, then uniform b in its half-slice); the canonical flag is recomputed by the exhaustive principal-ideal orbit oracle and compared with membership in the embedded pool; for the canonical ones Q_a, the exact norms (1/16 bit), primitivity (HNF of aO+bO), row and block lengths and the certified norm-bound block statistics (embedding_bounds, 64-cell blocks, width 128: evaluations, leaves, rejection) are compared with the embedded row, and the leaf bounds are checked to contain the exact norms. [3] exact metrics, lattice-count factors, eligible-a count, slice sizes. [4] retention/survivor models at the operating point, retained relation orbits vs excess x U, margin, pool standard error. [5] the cost model: per-cell instruction breakdown from the measured constants, relation collection, filtering ratio -> N, linear algebra. [6] filtering simulation at scale 2^13 at this profile (seed) and the embedded 2^17 table. [7] descent dynamic programme with the measured ECM multiplication, both logarithms, Markov bound at the cap. [8] mean number of degree-1 prime ideals per rational prime over the primes in [2^8, 2^12). [9] la_mac.s inner-loop count. Ledger: total_log2W_full_ledger, memory per job, sensitivities. Larger `samples` regenerates more of the pool (~20 ms per index).
